I’ll review the research plan and tracker, continue S07/T01, and update the summary with the findings and next steps.

S07/T01 asks for a section space containing both the theta source and the error being bounded. The earlier work rules out a generic first-order trace estimate. I’ll check which holomorphic and automorphy constraints survive the fourth-order source operator, with a separate reader checking the admissibility argument.

The fiber calculation gives a five-dimensional covariant theta-jet space with an explicit orthogonal basis. The complete source lies in it, but its ordinary lattice-cutoff residual generally does not. I’m adding a global cutoff construction and an explicit norm for the remaining error, so the contract covers an actual approximation residual. The base trace and physical error comparison remain obligations for T02.

The admissibility contract now includes a concrete source-cutoff residual, the fiber evaluation kernel, and the extra derivatives needed for its complement. It also explains why this is only an upper observation estimate: fiber membership alone can accommodate colliding sources. I’m checking the formulas and replaying the inherited collision controls before updating the task status.

The review found two wording issues, now corrected: the full five-jet class includes odd profiles, and the observation norm does not automatically dominate the covariant bulk norm. The cutoff residual also has both low and high jet components, so projecting away the low part would omit a real error term. The fresh control replay rejected all five event boxes and the separate signed Euler witness as expected.

S07/T01 is complete, and the overview, tracker, and summary are updated. The exact checks and separate internal review pass. S07/T02 is now Ready to price the selected residual against the direct method; a useful physical error improvement remains unproved.

Please continue with S07/T02
I’ll continue with the selected N=2 residual, compare its complete physical error payment with the direct source-tail method, and update the summary and tracker.

The profile norm sees a smooth cutoff error between lattice points that the physical path does not sample. That looks costly. I’m checking whether it gives a rigorous lower floor for this method’s assigned error allowance; if that floor exceeds the direct tail bound, it will justify stopping before an expensive approximation sweep.

The comparison is decisive. The selected trace rule’s assigned allowance has a lower floor more than 1,600 times the direct value-error allowance; the first-derivative comparison also loses by a wide margin. These are bounds on error payments, not on actual errors. I’m completing the uniform upper bounds, shared-tail accounting, and review before closing this specific attempt.

The independent review agrees with the scoped stopping decision. The bounds include the cutoff and base derivatives and the residual beyond the tube; both methods retain the same modes over the full half-line. I’m saving T02 as complete, with its benefit gate unmet. T03 stays Waiting for a different useful estimate.

Completed S07/T02 and updated the [summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/01_SYMMETRY_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_SUMMARY_20261019.md:556).

The selected profile-trace rule loses to direct tail allowances by factors exceeding **1,618** and **34,152**. Interval checks and internal review passed. This specific attempt is closed; S07/T03 remains Waiting for a useful estimate.
Ok so you don't recommend continuing with S07/T03 during this round?
I’ll check the recorded T03 gate against the T02 result before making that recommendation.

Correct. I recommend **leaving S07/T03 Waiting this round**. T02 completed its task by establishing a scoped failure; it did not deliver the useful estimate T03 requires.

This leaves S07 open. The next step would be a different observation estimate that preserves lattice sampling or signed cancellation. T03 should resume only after that estimate demonstrates an advantage in a bounded comparison.
Can you look into potential options for that, or was that part of earlier tasks?
I’ll check which alternatives were already assessed and which remain untested, then look for a bounded next step that addresses the loss found in T02.

The earlier plan named several alternatives, but T01/T02 tested only part of that list. Two cheap checks are now informative: moving the cutoff appears unable to rescue the unchanged trace rule, and projecting onto the five-jet space still leaves the same costly annulus in the complement. I’m checking those arguments and the remaining signed or adjoint options against work already completed in S03.

The remaining choices fall into two groups. Within S07, a signed or adjoint estimate for the complete corrected residual still needs a representation that adds something beyond S03’s existing endpoint formula. For practical certification, boundary winding is further along: its theorem and pilot exist, while a useful matched comparison remains unexecuted. I’m recording that distinction and the two new screens so the next round does not repeat them.

The assessment and checks are saved. I recommend a short representation audit of the complete signed residual as the next analytic step; boundary winding is the more mature option for a practical certification comparison. The two simple repairs to the old norm now have scoped failure proofs. T03 remains Waiting.

The earlier plan listed alternatives, but most were **proposals rather than completed tests**. I’ve now examined them further.

- **Signed or adjoint estimate:** Best next analytic step. Start with S03’s complete corrected residual and identify a new quantitative gain beyond its existing endpoint formula.
- **Boundary winding (GEO-T1):** Most developed practical alternative. Its theorem and pilot exist; a useful matched comparison remains unexecuted.
- **Cutoff tuning or finite-jet projection:** New checks show these still lose when retaining the old norm/complement payment. I would stop those variants.
- **Different form degrees:** Still exploratory and lower priority.

I saved the [assessment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/07_geometric_duality_and_quaternionic_symmetry/notes/05_OBSERVATION_OPTIONS_AND_BOUNDED_FEASIBILITY_SCREENS_20261019.md) and updated the summary. Let's continue with GEO-T1

I’ll review the GEO-T1 comparison gate and the existing winding pilot, select one bounded box from the documented certification bottleneck, and compare winding with direct certification under the same budget.

The documented bottleneck is the height-1000 box \(B\): earlier signed-strip certification needed a time-slab repair there. I’ll freeze that box and compare against a stronger direct baseline using the same complete source data. The shared source setup is likely to dominate total cost, so a faster boundary calculation may still miss the factor-two gate.

The first run certifies winding zero on the whole boundary of \(B\). The direct method also certifies \(B\), with fewer enclosure calls: 7 versus 10. Both spent about nine seconds on the shared source setup, and the boundary consumer was slightly slower. I’m checking the degree, coverage, and controls before recording the result.

The control checks behave as required: interior collisions give nonzero winding and are rejected; boundary events and unresolved uncertainty remain inconclusive. I’m finishing the two-precision comparison and a separate replay, then recording the result and stopping decision in the summary.

Both precisions give the same result: winding zero certifies \(B\), and direct certification covers it with three strips. Including source setup, the methods take about 9–10 seconds each, so winding falls well short of the factor-two cost target. The separate replay agrees with the saved mathematical record.

The result note, review, tracker and summary are saved. Final checks confirm complete boundary and direct coverage, matching source records, and all 36 controls at both precisions. GEO-T1 is complete as a bounded validation; the cost gate failed, so the fixed-box comparison stops and S07-T3 remains waiting.

GEO-T1 is complete. Winding zero certifies the selected box, but optimized direct certification also succeeds with fewer calls: **7 versus 10**. Setup dominates both costs, so the factor-two cost target fails; no new coverage was gained.
